section.book: Bittinger, Beecher, Ellenbogen & Penna, College Algebra: Graphs and Models, 7e
section.title: Analyzing Graphs of Quadratic Functions

title: Maximum height of a launched object, s(t) = -16t^2 + v t + h0
sources: OpenStax College Algebra 2e §5.1 Example 9 p. 403 (CC BY 4.0): method only

problem.prompt: An object is launched upward at {v} ft/sec from {h0} ft. Its height after t sec is s(t) = {tex:s}. When does it reach its maximum height, and what is that height?

steps.name: identify the coefficients (a and b with their signs)
compute the time with the vertex formula
substitute to find the maximum height

answer.say: It reaches its maximum height of {s0} ft after {t0} sec.

mistakes.name: swapped time and height
mistakes.message: The vertex is (time, height): t first, then s(t).

mistakes.name: dropped the minus in -b/(2a)
mistakes.message: t = -b/(2a) = -v/(2(-16)) is positive; a negative time means a sign slip.

hints.step: identify the coefficients (a and b with their signs)
hints.why: The vertex formula uses a and b.

hints.step: compute the time with the vertex formula
hints.why: The highest point is the vertex.

hints.step: substitute to find the maximum height
hints.why: The maximum height is the y-coordinate of the vertex.

hints.hint: Height in ft, time in sec.
